claims.text: The CrFeNiMo, Co0.5CrFeNiMo, and Al0.5CrFeNiMo powders are mechanically alloyed for 30 h with N-heptane and sieved to ≤80 µm.
The low-carbon C1018 steel substrates are polished and degreased before coating.
The proposed high SPS temperatures are 1050 °C for CrFeNiMo, 1000 °C for Co0.5CrFeNiMo, and 950 °C for Al0.5CrFeNiMo.
Increasing SPS temperature enhances particle diffusion.
Increasing SPS temperature enhances homogenization of the consolidated alloys.
Increasing SPS temperature improves densification and lowers porosity.
Higher-temperature SPS produces a refined multiphase microstructure.
A six-layer ESD coating provides more continuous surface coverage than a three-layer ESD coating.
A six-layer ESD coating adheres or bonds better to C1018 steel than a three-layer coating.
Six-layer ESD coatings may exhibit minor oxidation and microfissuring.
Enhanced diffusion and alloying during SPS improve particle sintering.
Reduced porosity creates a more mechanically robust microstructure.
Combining higher-temperature SPS with six-layer ESD increases surface hardness relative to lower-temperature SPS with three-layer ESD.
Combining higher-temperature SPS with six-layer ESD produces a denser coating with lower porosity than the baseline process.
Combining higher-temperature SPS with six-layer ESD produces a more homogeneous coating than the baseline process.
The combined intervention improves mechanical performance under conditions simulating aggressive environments.
The proposed benefits for corrosion and wear resistance during actual aggressive-environment exposure have not been directly validated.
Microstructural observations support the proposed mechanism for enhanced densification and hardness.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as an 'untreated or lower-performance baseline,' but it actually receives both SPS consolidation and a three-layer ESD coating, so it is not untreated.
